clue.text: Playwright's one Cold War novel

indicators.note: novel as an adjective means new or fresh, so the letters before it are put into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A dramatist is said to have written a single book set during the Cold War.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a noun after 'Cold War', but it is the anagram signal: ONE and COLDWAR are rearranged together. The 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: The English dramatist behind Private Lives and Blithe Spirit is a famous man of the theatre.

clue.text: Binge read, hiding covers when in public

indicators.note: in places the trimmed word inside the word for public

parts.note: something done in public is overt, open to view

indicators.note: the word read with its covers hidden keeps only the letters between its first and last

explanation.surface: Someone reads greedily in public, keeping the book covers out of sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hiding covers' strips R and D from READ to leave EA, which goes 'in' OVERT; 'when' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To binge is to consume food to excess, eating more than one should.

clue.text: O'Neill regularly brought up Tolstoy

indicators.note: brought up in a down clue means the picked letters are read from bottom to top
regularly takes every other letter of the name, starting with the first

explanation.surface: The American playwright O'Neill often mentioned the Russian novelist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes O, E, L from O'NEILL; 'brought up' turns them round, as befits a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Count Tolstoy's first name was Lev, rendered in English as this Latin-looking form.

clue.text: Lines of praise regarding theatre

parts.note: an ode is a lyric poem addressing and praising its subject
on means about or concerning, as in a book on birds

explanation.surface: Verses honouring something are written about the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: The British cinema chain's name, from a Greek word for a hall for music, also names a theatre or concert hall.

clue.text: Dimwit oddly engrossed by rise of Lara Croft in Kellynch Hall?

indicators.note: engrossed by means the odd letters are absorbed inside the turned name
rise of in a down clue means the name Lara is read upwards
oddly takes the first, third and fifth letters of the word dimwit

explanation.surface: A fool is captivated by the rise of the video game heroine Lara Croft in a stately home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rise of' turns LARA into ARAL; 'oddly' takes DMI from DIMWIT, which is 'engrossed by' it. In Austen's Persuasion, Admiral Croft rents Kellynch Hall from Sir Walter Elliot.
explanation.definitionFit: The naval officer who leases the Elliots' house in Persuasion holds this flag rank.

clue.text: Philosopher Mark has time to get into review of source

indicators.note: to get into signals the mark and time going inside the turned word
review taken as re-view, looking again from the other end, turns the synonym backwards

parts.note: seed is a source, the thing from which something grows
a scar is a mark left on the skin

explanation.surface: A thinker with a blemish takes time to review where something came from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'review of' turns SEED into DEES, and SCAR plus T go 'to get into' it; 'has' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The French thinker of 'I think, therefore I am' is a founding figure of modern philosophy.

clue.text: Following a common character pairing in Falstaff and Mistress Quickly

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

parts.words: common character pairing in Falstaff and Mistress
parts.note: the letter pair S then T appears in both Falstaff and Mistress

explanation.surface: Two Shakespeare characters, Sir John Falstaff and Mistress Quickly of the Boar's Head tavern, are presented as a stock pairing.
explanation.walkthrough: Mistress Quickly is the hostess in Shakespeare's Henry IV plays, but here 'Quickly' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving fast means moving with speed, a synonym of acting rapidly.

clue.text: Description of Adam's narrative style

parts.note: Adam was the earliest human in Genesis, and a story told with 'I' as narrator has a grammatical label that also fits him

explanation.surface: A critic sums up how a novelist named Adam tells his stories.
explanation.definitionFit: Narration using 'I' is named for the grammatical form, which also describes the earliest human being.

clue.text: My son's off touring New York State for report?

indicators.note: touring means going around, so the jumbled letters surround the abbreviation
off here means gone wrong, so the letters of the words are jumbled

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written
NY is the postal abbreviation for New York State

explanation.surface: A parent says their boy has left to travel round New York State to write an account.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My son's' is 'my son is'; 'off' jumbles MYSON and the result goes 'touring' NY. The question mark marks the definition as an example: 'account' could stand for 'report'.
explanation.definitionFit: A word that can stand in for another, as account does in place of report, is its equivalent term.

clue.text: In character, one leers over rare and radiant maiden

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the concealed letters read from right to left
In signals that the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: In a story, some character leers at a beautiful young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading 'character, one leers' backwards gives SREELENORETC, and LENORE sits inside it. The definition quotes Poe's poem The Raven.
explanation.definitionFit: Poe's narrator mourns his lost love as 'the rare and radiant maiden whom the angels name' by this name.

clue.text: Savagely rips into brand-new book's error

indicators.note: into places the jumbled letters inside the word for brand-new

parts.note: in mint condition means brand-new, never used

indicators.note: savagely means wildly and roughly, so the word rips is torn into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone tears violently into a new book because of a mistake in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Savagely' turns RIPS into SPRI, which goes 'into' MINT.
explanation.definitionFit: A typographical slip in a printed volume is a classic printing mistake.

clue.text: Booker winner can tolerate no changes

indicators.note: changes as a noun signals that the letters of the phrase are altered into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A prize-winning novelist is unable to put up with any revisions.
explanation.definitionFit: The New Zealand author won the 2013 Man Booker Prize for The Luminaries.

clue.text: Final sign of apocalypse hasn't started: time to get support

parts.note: the end is the final part

indicators.note: hasn't started means the first letter is dropped from the word for the riders

parts.note: the Four Horsemen of Revelation herald the end of the world

explanation.surface: The last portent of doomsday hasn't begun, so it is time to get backing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hasn't started' takes H off HORSEMEN, the riders of Revelation, leaving ORSEMEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Backing a cause publicly is giving it approval and support.

clue.text: Movie company starts to film loose adaptation, transforming A Room of One's Own?

parts.note: a film studio is a company that makes movies

indicators.note: starts to takes the first letter of each following word

explanation.surface: A film company takes on a free adaptation of Virginia Woolf's essay.
explanation.walkthrough: Woolf's essay title is reread literally: a single room of your own is a one-room home.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-room apartment is literally a room that a person has to themselves.

clue.text: 1950s tale about work of McCarthy

parts.note: on means about, as in a talk on art
Cormac McCarthy wrote the 2006 post-apocalyptic novel The Road

explanation.surface: A story from the 1950s is about a book by Cormac McCarthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'McCarthy' suggests the 1950s senator, but it is the novelist Cormac McCarthy.
explanation.definitionFit: Kerouac's Beat novel was published in 1957.

clue.text: Flaubert protagonist's a madame, on reflection

indicators.note: on reflection means seen as in a mirror, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: Mme is the standard abbreviation for the French title madame

explanation.surface: Flaubert's heroine is a married French lady, when you think about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on reflection' turns A + MME round. The 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: The heroine of Madame Bovary bears this first name.

clue.text: Othello in Brontë country?

definitions.meaning: Shakespeare's Othello is subtitled the Venetian general of North African origin
the Yorkshire landscape of Wuthering Heights is open upland heath

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's general turns up in Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's general is a North African, and the Brontës' Yorkshire is wild open heathland.

clue.text: Shifted more copies than Oxford University Press: finally informed stores

indicators.note: stores means holds inside, so the word for informed holds the picked letter

parts.note: told means informed, as in told the police

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word press

explanation.surface: A university publisher reports that its sales beat a rival's.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oxford University Press' reads as one publisher but splits into three parts; 'finally' acts on 'Press', and 'stores' puts that letter inside the word for informed.
explanation.definitionFit: A book that beat another in sales was sold in greater numbers.

clue.text: This week's TLS perhaps follows Keats translation contests

indicators.note: follows places the magazine word after the rearranged name
translation means turning into another form, so the poet's name is rearranged

parts.note: a weekly magazine's current number is its issue

explanation.surface: The current literary magazine follows a translation of Keats.
explanation.definitionFit: To dispute or challenge a claim is to object to it.

clue.text: What's missing from children's title? Something like cricket

indicators.note: missing from means the first word is removed from the book title

parts.note: What Katy Did is Susan Coolidge's classic 1872 children's book

explanation.surface: A puzzle asks what has gone from a children's book, and offers an insect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What's' is 'What is': take WHAT off WHAT KATY DID. A cricket is an insect here, not the sport.
explanation.definitionFit: This green North American bush insect is a relative of grasshoppers, named for its call.

clue.text: Homer's Y-fronts in Simpsons ineptly lost upon dressing

indicators.note: dressing means clothing, so the word upon wraps around the picked letters
fronts in takes the front letter of each of the next three words

explanation.surface: Homer Simpson's underpants are clumsily lost on a character getting dressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Homer' is the Greek poet, not Homer Simpson: Y in Greek is the letter written in his alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek alphabet's twentieth character, written like a Y, is what the epic poet's language uses.

clue.text: Old and new books? This sequel arrived after 34 years

definitions.meaning: the Bible's two halves, the Old and New collections of books
Atwood's 2019 sequel to The Handmaid's Tale, published 34 years after the 1985 original

explanation.surface: The Bible's two halves are set beside a long-awaited follow-up novel.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bible's two divisions and Margaret Atwood's 2019 follow-up novel share the same title.

clue.text: "What passion cannot — raise and quell?' (Dryden, "A Song for St. Cecilia's Day")

definitions.text: What passion cannot — raise and quell?' (Dryden, "A Song for St. Cecilia's Day")

parts.words: What passion cannot — raise and quell?' (Dryden, "A Song for St. Cecilia's Day")
parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation: the missing word is the art St Cecilia is patron of

explanation.definitionFit: Dryden's ode for the patron saint of musicians praises melody and harmony as able to stir any feeling.

clue.text: Parade's End line recalled in its author's preface

indicators.note: in places the pieces inside the novelist's surname

parts.note: Parade's End was written by Ford Madox Ford

indicators.note: End picks the last letter of the word parade
recalled means called back, so the word for line runs backwards

parts.note: a row is a line of things side by side

explanation.surface: A line from Parade's End is remembered in the introduction its novelist wrote.
explanation.walkthrough: The novel title 'Parade's End' is split so that 'End' acts on 'Parade's'; 'recalled' turns the line round, and 'in' puts both inside the surname of the novel's author, Ford Madox Ford.
explanation.definitionFit: An introductory piece at the front of a book is its introduction.

clue.text: Jonson wrote this of news wire for papers

definitions.meaning: Ben Jonson's 1626 comedy is The ... of News
a bent wire clip fastening sheets of paper together

explanation.surface: A playwright wrote about news, and a wire holds papers together.
explanation.definitionFit: Ben Jonson's comedy title supplies the word, and a bent metal clip fastens sheets together.

clue.text: How to be both Smith, and the sportsman he portrayed?

definitions.meaning: the author of the novel How to Be Both is ... Smith
Will Smith played the boxer Muhammad in the 2001 film about him

explanation.surface: A question asks how one person can be both an author named Smith and the athlete he played.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish novelist's first name matches the surname of the heavyweight boxing champion played by Will Smith.

clue.text: Prepare to publish abridgement of Wharton

indicators.note: abridgement of means shortening, so the last letter is cut off the first name

parts.note: Edith Wharton was the American novelist of The Age of Innocence

explanation.surface: An editor gets ready to print a shortened version of Wharton.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wharton' stands for her first name; cutting its last letter, H, is the 'abridgement'.
explanation.definitionFit: To revise and correct a text is the work of getting it ready for print.

clue.text: Duo trailing Lestrade discount suspect that Holmes delivered

indicators.note: duo trailing means the final two letters of the inspector's name
suspect as an adjective means dubious or unsound, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A pair of detectives follows Inspector Lestrade and dismisses a suspect, as Holmes would have done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duo trailing' takes DE from LESTRADE; 'suspect' scrambles DISCOUNT into DUCTIONS. 'suspect' looks like a noun but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Sherlock Holmes's famous conclusions were reasoned inferences drawn from clues.
